keykeeperImportCheckNotStarted.message: Your items couldn't be read to check this import, so nothing was imported. Try again.

keykeeperImportCheckNotRead.message: The import finished, but its items couldn't be read back to be checked. Reload, then look in the items you imported for fields whose names start with "keykeeper." and delete those fields.

keykeeperImportCheckTrashed.message: The import finished, but these items have fields whose names start with "keykeeper." that couldn't be changed, so they're in the trash: $NAMES$.

keykeeperImportCheckNotSaved.message: The import finished, but these items have fields whose names start with "keykeeper." that couldn't be changed, and the items couldn't be moved to the trash: $NAMES$. Delete them.

keykeeperImportCheckMissing.message: The import finished, but only $CHECKED$ of its $TOTAL$ items could be checked. Look in the others for fields whose names start with "keykeeper." and delete those fields.

keykeeperExpiringItemsReportDesc.message: Items that have expired or expire in the next 30 days: API keys, certificates, licenses, cards, and anything you set an expiration date on.

keykeeperNoExpiringItems.message: No items have expired or expire in the next 30 days.

keykeeperExpiringItemsFoundDesc.message: These items have expired or expire in the next 30 days. Renew or rotate them, then update their expiration dates.

keykeeperMemberHealthReportDesc.message: How many of each member's own logins, in their Personal items, have weak, reused, or exposed passwords.

keykeeperMemberHealthPrivacy.message: Each member's apps count their own logins and send only these numbers. Neither you nor the server sees which logins, their names, or their passwords. This organization's items are in the other reports.

keykeeperMemberHealthCouldntLoad.message: The numbers couldn't be loaded. Try again later.

keykeeperMemberHealthNotReported.message: Not reported yet: their apps send the numbers after they next unlock.

keykeeperMemberHealthExposedNote.message: Exposed passwords are counted only by the web vault, while its breach check is on. Members who use only the browser extension or the apps show Not checked.

keykeeperMemberHealthTotals.message: In their own items: $WEAK$ weak and $REUSED$ reused passwords.

keykeeperOwnHealthSeenBy.message: Owners and admins of the organizations you're a member of see how many of your own passwords are weak, reused, or exposed. Never which ones.

keykeeperVersionsUnreadable.message: Earlier versions that can't be opened: $COUNT$

keykeeperRestoreVersionDesc.message: The item goes back to how it was on $DATE$. How it is now stays in its version history, so you can come back to it.

keykeeperVersionSameAsNow.message: This version looks the same as the item does now.

keykeeperVersionHistoryWhoSees.message: Everyone who can open this item can see its earlier versions, including old passwords.

keykeeperVersionHistoryHiddenPasswords.message: You can't see this item's passwords, so its earlier versions show only when they were saved and by whom.

keykeeperClearHistoryDesc.message: Its earlier versions are deleted for everyone who can open it. The item stays as it is now.

keykeeperDeleteVersionDesc.message: The version from $DATE$ is deleted for everyone who can open this item.

keykeeperClearedHistoryItemId.message: Cleared the earlier versions of item $ID$.

keykeeperEventStreamAdded.message: Started sending the organization's events to a new place.

keykeeperEventStreamChanged.message: Changed a place the organization's events are sent.

keykeeperEventStreamRemoved.message: Stopped sending the organization's events to a place.

keykeeperEventStreamStopped.message: The server turned off a place the organization's events are sent: sending there kept failing.

keykeeperDeletedVersionItemId.message: Deleted an earlier version of item $ID$.

keykeeperManageAccountRecoveryHint.message: Can reset the master password of members in account recovery, and so sign in as them and see everything they can.

keykeeperImportExportHint.message: Covers import. Exporting the organization's items takes access to all of them, which owners and admins have and custom roles don't, so an owner or admin exports.

keykeeperCustomRoleNoCollections.message: A custom role with these permissions gets its shared folders one by one: choose them on the Shared folders tab. To reach every shared folder, make them an admin instead.

keykeeperBiometricsNotEnrolled.message: Unlock with biometrics is still off. It wasn't confirmed, or the desktop app isn't running.

keykeeperSelfHostedAddressHint.message: Your server's address, such as vault.example.com.

keykeeperAccessIntro.message: Who can open each shared folder, and how. Owners and admins see every item. Everyone else opens the shared folders they're given, directly or through a group. Someone who reaches a folder two ways gets, for each permission, the more open way, so passwords stay hidden only if every way hides them.

keykeeperAccessHiddenFolder.message: 1 shared folder isn't shown, since you can't open it yourself.

keykeeperAccessHiddenFolders.message: $COUNT$ shared folders aren't shown, since you can't open them yourself.

keykeeperAccessSearch.message: Search people, groups, and shared folders

keykeeperAccessEveryItemPeople.message: Also open to everyone who sees every item: $NAMES$.

keykeeperAccessOnlyEveryItemPeople.message: Only people who see every item can open it: $NAMES$.

keykeeperAccessNoFoldersYet.message: This organization has no shared folders yet.

keykeeperAccessLoadFailed.message: Couldn't load who can see what. Reload the page to try again.

keykeeperCanViewHidden.message: Can view but not see passwords

keykeeperCanEditHidden.message: Can edit but not see passwords

keykeeperCapSeePasswordsHint.message: Passwords, codes, card numbers, and ID numbers. Without it, people can still fill these into web pages, and a page can read what's filled.

keykeeperGridAppsEnforce.message: The server enforces the rest; see passwords, export, share, and print are up to the apps, since anyone who can open an item could copy it with other tools.

keykeeperGridManageIncludesAll.message: Managing a shared folder includes every other permission in it.

keykeeperGridNeedsSeePasswords.message: Export, print, and share need see passwords.

keykeeperReachFoldersRevoked.message: Before they were revoked, $NAME$ could open $FOLDERS$ with $ITEMS$.

keykeeperReachEveryItem.message: $NAME$ can see every item in this organization: $ITEMS$.

keykeeperReachEveryItemRevoked.message: Before they were revoked, $NAME$ could see every item in this organization: $ITEMS$.

keykeeperReachNoFoldersRevoked.message: Before they were revoked, $NAME$ couldn't open any shared folders.

keykeeperReachNeverConfirmed.message: $NAME$ was never confirmed, so they never had the key to this organization's items.

keykeeperSeenPasswordsIntro.message: $NAME$ could see these logins' passwords in the shared folders they could open. They may still know them, so change them.

keykeeperSeenPasswordsEveryItem.message: $NAME$ could see every item in this organization, so they may know any of its passwords.

keykeeperSeenPasswordsOtherItems.message: Other items they could see, such as notes and cards, aren't listed.

keykeeperSeenPasswordsNotAgain.message: This list won't be shown again, so copy it if you'll need it later.

keykeeperSeenPasswordsAccessLink.message: See who can open each shared folder

keykeeperSeenPasswordsIntroMany.message: $NAMES$ could see these logins' passwords in the shared folders they could open. They may still know them, so change them.

keykeeperSeenPasswordsEveryItemMany.message: $NAMES$ could see every item in this organization, so they may know any of its passwords.

keykeeperExposedPrivacy.message: Each password is checked against Have I Been Pwned's list of breached passwords without sending it: only the first 5 characters of its SHA-1 hash leave your browser, the answer lists hundreds of possible matches, and the match is made here.

keykeeperExposedUnchecked.message: $COUNT$ items couldn't be checked for breaches, because this browser couldn't reach api.pwnedpasswords.com. It may be offline, or a firewall may block it. Try again later.

keykeeperHealthToFix.message: $COUNT$ items to fix: weak, reused, or exposed passwords, or items that expire soon

keykeeperExposedCheckFailed.message: Couldn't check this password, because this browser couldn't reach api.pwnedpasswords.com. It may be offline, or a firewall may block it.

keykeeperBreachCheckAfterUnlock.message: Check my passwords against known breaches after unlocking

keykeeperBreachCheckAfterUnlockHint.message: For the count beside Health (for MSP staff, every client item you can edit) and the MSP console's Exposed column. Each check sends Have I Been Pwned the first 5 characters of each password's SHA-1 hash. Turned off, nothing is sent unless you open the exposed passwords report or press Check. Creating or changing your master password checks it the same way while "Check known data breaches for this password" is ticked there, as it is at first.

keykeeperHealthToFixOne.message: 1 item to fix: a weak, reused, or exposed password, or an item that expires soon

keykeeperExposedUncheckedOne.message: 1 item couldn't be checked for breaches, because this browser couldn't reach api.pwnedpasswords.com. It may be offline, or a firewall may block it. Try again later.

keykeeperServerAddressHint.message: Just the address. We add https:// for you.

keykeeperServerAddressInvalid.message: That isn't a server address. Try one like vault.example.com.

keykeeperNewHereInvite.message: New here? Your admin sends the invite.

keykeeperServerAddressOnly.message: Use just the server's address, without @, ? or #.

keykeeperServerUnreachable.message: Couldn't reach a server at that address. Check it for typos, and that you're online.

keykeeperServerSlow.message: The server at that address didn't answer in time. Check the address, then try again.

keykeeperServerNotAServer.message: There's no $BRAND$ server at that address. Check it for typos.

keykeeperServerBroken.message: The server at that address had a problem. Try again in a few minutes, or ask whoever runs it.

keykeeperCustomServerAddresses.message: This browser uses custom server addresses.

keykeeperRestoreVersionDropsPasskey.message: The item goes back to how it was on $DATE$. How it is now stays in its version history, so you can come back to it. This version doesn't have its passkey for $PASSKEY$: restoring removes it, and you can't sign in with it after.

keykeeperRestoreVersionDropsPasskeys.message: The item goes back to how it was on $DATE$. How it is now stays in its version history, so you can come back to it. This version doesn't have $COUNT$ of its passkeys (for $PASSKEYS$): restoring removes them, and you can't sign in with them after.

keykeeperRestoreFailed.message: Couldn't restore it. If the item changed since you opened it, go back and try again.

keykeeperCantMoveItem.message: Your organization doesn't let you move it to another shared folder.

keykeeperCantCopyItem.message: Your organization doesn't let you copy this item.

keykeeperSsoLinkInWebVault.message: Your organization requires single sign-on, and your account isn't linked to it yet. Sign in to the web vault with your email and master password to link it, then sign in here with single sign-on.

keykeeperLinkSsoVerify.message: Confirm it's you to link your account to this organization's single sign-on. Microsoft then asks which account to use, and you confirm it before anything is linked.

keykeeperTwoStepSetupInWebVault.message: Two-step login is required for your role by $NAMES$. Sign in to the web vault at $URL$ to set it up with an authenticator app, a security key or passkey, or Duo, then sign in here again.

keykeeperTwoStepSetupInWebVaultUnnamed.message: Two-step login is required for your role. Sign in to the web vault at $URL$ to set it up with an authenticator app, a security key or passkey, or Duo, then sign in here again.

keykeeperAdminTwoStepOn.message: Turned on two-step login for admins.

keykeeperAdminTwoStepOff.message: Turned off two-step login for admins.

keykeeperEveryoneTwoStepOff.message: Stopped requiring two-step login of everyone, so it's required for admins only.

keykeeperAdminTwoStepPolicyDesc.message: Owners, admins, and custom roles that manage members, policies, or account recovery must use an authenticator app, a security key or passkey, or Duo. Email codes don't count. Admins who sign in with the organization's own single sign-on are covered by it there.

keykeeperConfirmProvisioningToken.message: Confirm it's you to make a provisioning token. Whoever has it can add and remove people in this organization.

keykeeperConfirmSsoSettings.message: Confirm it's you to save the single sign-on settings, which decide how people in this organization sign in.

keykeeperConfirmEventDestination.message: Confirm it's you to change where events are sent.

keykeeperConfirmSigningSecret.message: Confirm it's you to make a new signing secret.

keykeeperConfirmScriptToken.message: Confirm it's you to make this script token. Scripts with it can read the fields you chose.

keykeeperConfirmAdminTwoStep.message: Confirm it's you to change whether this organization's admins must use two-step login.

keykeeperConfirmStaffTwoStep.message: Confirm it's you to change whether your staff must use two-step login.

keykeeperSsoForCommandLine.message: This signs in the command-line tool on this computer. Continue only if you started that sign-in yourself, just now.

keykeeperOpenAndFillHint.message: Open and fill doesn't need this setting: the open button beside a login opens its website in a new tab and fills it there, once, and only on that site. It never submits the form.

keykeeperDuoBackToAppDesc.message: Your browser opens the app to finish signing in. If it doesn't, select Back to the app.

keykeeperFolderLookPreview.message: How it shows in the menu

keykeeperFolderLookHint.message: Everyone who has this folder sees its icon. It's encrypted, like the folder's name.

keykeeperPasswordChangeConfirmText.message: A new tab opens the site's change-password page. A new password is saved to this item first, then filled in and submitted. The old one stays in password history, and one click puts it back.

keykeeperPasswordChangeNotStartedRunning.message: Another password change is still running. Finish it or close its tab first.

keykeeperPasswordChangeNotStartedNotAllo.message: This item's password can't be changed here.

keykeeperPasswordChangeNotStartedNoWebsi.message: This item needs an https website to change its password on.

keykeeperPasswordChangeUnsureText.message: On $DATE$, this item got a new password for $SITE$, but it isn't clear whether the site took it. Try signing in to the site with the new password.

keykeeperPasswordChangeRefusedTitle.message: The site didn't take the new password

keykeeperPasswordChangeRefusedText.message: On $DATE$, $SITE$ didn't take this item's new password, so the site still has the old one. Put the old password back so the item matches the site.

keykeeperPasswordChangePutBackDone.message: The old password is back. The new one is in password history.

keykeeperPasswordChangeItWorkedDone.message: Saved. The item keeps the new password.

keykeeperPasswordChangeSaveFailed.message: The item couldn't be saved. Open it again and try once more.

keykeeperPasswordChangeFinding.message: Looking for the change-password form on $SITE$.

keykeeperPasswordChangeSignIn.message: Sign in to $SITE$ first. This carries on when the change-password form shows.

keykeeperPasswordChangeNoForm.message: There's no change-password form on this page. Go to the site's change-password page in this tab, and this carries on there.

keykeeperPasswordChangeCaptchaFirst.message: The site wants you to prove you're not a robot. Do that, and this carries on when the change-password form shows.

keykeeperPasswordChangeSaving.message: Saving a new password to the item first.

keykeeperPasswordChangeHandoverCaptcha.message: The site wants you to prove you're not a robot. Do that, then submit the form. The new password is saved and filled in.

keykeeperPasswordChangeHandoverCode.message: The site asks for a code. Enter it, then submit the form. The new password is saved and filled in.

keykeeperPasswordChangeHandoverEmail.message: The site sent you a message to confirm the change. Follow it to finish, then open the item to say whether it worked.

keykeeperPasswordChangeHandoverForm.message: Finish the rest of the form, then submit it. The new password is saved and filled in.

keykeeperPasswordChangeHandoverButton.message: Submit the form to finish. The new password is saved and filled in.

keykeeperPasswordChangeChanged.message: Password changed. The new one is saved in the item.

keykeeperPasswordChangeRefused.message: $SITE$ didn't take the new password. Open the item to put the old one back.

keykeeperPasswordChangeUnsure.message: It isn't clear whether $SITE$ took the new password. Open the item to say whether it worked.

keykeeperPasswordChangeStoppedClosed.message: The tab closed, so the password change stopped. Nothing was changed.

keykeeperPasswordChangeStoppedElsewhere.message: The tab went to another site, so the password change stopped. Nothing was changed.

keykeeperPasswordChangeStoppedLocked.message: Locked, so the password change stopped. Nothing was changed.

keykeeperPasswordChangeStoppedGone.message: The item is gone, so the password change stopped. Nothing was changed.

keykeeperPasswordChangeStoppedTimeout.message: No change-password form showed up in time, so this stopped. Nothing was changed.

keykeeperPasswordChangeStoppedNoCurrent.message: This form doesn't ask for the current password, so it may not be for your own account. Nothing was changed. Change the password yourself.

keykeeperPasswordChangeStoppedAmbiguous.message: This page has more than one form like this, so it isn't clear which one to use. Nothing was changed. Change the password yourself.

keykeeperPasswordChangeStoppedRules.message: No password fits this site's rules, so nothing was changed.

keykeeperPasswordChangeStoppedChangedMea.message: The item changed since you started, so this stopped. Nothing was changed.

keykeeperPasswordChangeStoppedSaveFailed.message: The new password couldn't be saved, so nothing was changed on the site.

keykeeperPasswordChangeElsewhereAfterSav.message: The tab went to another site after the new password was saved. Open the item to say whether it worked.

keykeeperPasswordChangeLockedAfterSave.message: Locked after the new password was saved. Unlock and open the item to say whether it worked.

keykeeperPasswordChangedItemId.message: Changed the password of item $ID$ on its website.

keykeeperPasswordPutBackItemId.message: Put back the earlier password of item $ID$ after a password change.

keykeeperPasswordChangeOffPolicyDesc.message: Change password in the browser extension won't change the passwords of this organization's items on their sites. It only opens the site's change-password page, and people change it themselves.

keykeeperBrowserAutofillUnchangedEvent.message: Left the browsers' card and address autofill as they are.

keykeeperBrowserAutofillOffEvent.message: Turned off the browsers' card and address autofill.

keykeeperBrowserAutofillOffAndImportEven.message: Turned off the browsers' card and address autofill, offering to bring them in.

keykeeperBrowserAutofillOffPolicy.message: Turn off the browsers' card and address autofill

keykeeperBrowserAutofillOffPolicyDesc.message: Chrome, Edge, and Firefox stop saving and filling cards and addresses in people's work profiles, and on computers the install command set up. What they saved stays in the browser.
